title: SummitCare - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share onboarding deck and implementation checklist (Maya) by 2027-03-12
Customer to provide network/VPC diagram and security contact (Carlos) by 2027-03-16
Schedule technical deep dive for private deployment with SE and customer infra team (Ethan to propose times)
action_items: Ethan: prepare private deployment checklist and sample kv-cache sizing spreadsheet (due 2027-03-15)
Carlos: upload VPC diagram and internal firewall rules to shared folder (due 2027-03-16)
Priya: setup weekly checkpoint meeting invite (ongoing)
summary: Kickoff for SummitCare onboarding to Redwood. Discussed host vs dedicated vs private options, security controls (KMS, SSO, audit logs), timeline for pilot, integration points (API vs SDK), and next steps for artifacts and technical deep dive. Customer expressed interest in private deployment or dedicated capacity due to PHI/data residency concerns; agreed to run initial pilot on hosted with strict retention + audit logs while evaluating Private deployment requirements.
transcript:
Header: 2027-03-11 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Dr. Amir (CTO), Lena (Head of ML), Carlos (DevOps), Sofia (Product)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya with redwood inference, i'm the AE on this account, we also have ethan our se and priya cs manager. quick round-robin?
00:12 Amir: sure, amir here, CTO at summitcare, i'll be the exec sponsor.
00:18 Lena: lena, head of ml, i'll own the integration and eval.
00:24 Carlos: carlos, devops, i'll handle networking and infra.
00:30 Priya: great, thanks. high level we want to run through onboarding plan, security asks, and a pilot scope.
00:42 Maya: perfect. quick agenda: intro, goals, security/compliance, integration points, pilot success criteria and timeline, next steps. sound good?
00:52 Amir: yes, go ahead.
01:05 Ethan: i'll kick off with the options we usually propose — hosted api for fastest time-to-value, dedicated capacity for predictable throughput/data isolation, and private (vpc/on-prem) for regulated workloads. note: we recommend starting with hosted pilot if you want results quickly, while we size up dedicated/private.
01:28 Lena: we have PHI, so data residency and encryption at rest/in transit are musts. Also SSO for devs and audit logging for compliance.
01:38 Maya: totally, that's common. Redwood supports SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and KMS integrations. for private we do a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package.
01:52 Carlos: can you share more on KMS integration? we use AWS KMS and use an HSM for key rotation in some pockets.
02:01 Ethan: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and can support customer-managed keys. small caveat: if you go hosted with customer-managed keys, there are additional steps around key grants; we'll share the exact config in the security pack.
02:18 Maya: i'll drop the security-pack.pdf and onboarding-deck into the shared drive after this call.
02:25 Amir: timeline — looking for pilot in 6 weeks, production in Q3. is that feasible?
02:35 Ethan: feasible. typical path: week 0-2 network and auth setup, week 2-4 integration + test prompts, week 4-6 run benchmarks and quality checks, week 6 decide on dedicated/private and start rollout. if you need private on-prem, add provisioning & infra validation time.
03:00 Lena: for the pilot we want throughput ~50rps and p95 latency under 500ms for chat use cases; cost is also a big constraint.
03:12 Ethan: ok, that makes sense. p95 <500ms is doable on dedicated or tuned hosted endpoints depending on model and sequence lengths. we'll recommend model/quantization options and batching config in the kv-cache sizing sheet.
03:30 Carlos: networking question — if we go private, does redwood need peering, transit gateway, or do you recommend a private connect?
03:38 Ethan: options: vpc peering for simpler setups, or AWS TGW / VPN for enterprise. we also support static egress IP ranges for allowlisting. i'll include recommended network topologies.
03:52 Sofia: any differences in observability between hosted and private? we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
04:02 Priya: yes, the console exposes token-level cost, latency breakdowns, traces and can forward logs to your SIEM. retention for hosted is configurable as an add-on, for private you control retention.
04:18 Lena: about data retention — during pilot we need data purged daily and we need audit logs retained for 1 year.
04:25 Maya: we can set retention policies and provide audit exports. for hosted pilot we'll enable short retention and enable object-level purging, and we can confirm log retention SLA in the security doc.
04:40 Amir: ok good. how do we do model versioning and rollouts? we want safe rollouts, canary and rollback.
04:49 Ethan: built-in rollout features: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to model variant. we'll help you configure policies. Also we can tie quality monitoring to your evaluation sets so regressions alert you.
05:05 Lena: for evaluation we have a labeled set of 2k prompts, can redwood run quality regressions against that?
05:12 Ethan: yes, we can run evals and wire alerts. we'll need the prompt set and expected outputs; we can run an initial baseline during the pilot.
05:24 Carlos: procurement question — what does pricing look like for dedicated vs private?
05:30 Maya: short answer: dedicated is reserved capacity commit (monthly/annual), private is platform fee + support; we'll send detailed pricing and a sample TCO spreadsheet. pricing will depend on throughput and model choices.
05:45 Amir: competitors — we've talked to anthropic and bedrock. they're in the mix.
05:50 Maya: noted, we'll highlight differentiators: production-first runtime, transparent benchmarks, and cost-aware controls like caching and recommended quantization.
06:05 Ethan: technical note on caching — we support prefix caching and kv-cache to reduce per-token cost; for chat workloads we'll discuss strategies to preserve latency while batching.
06:20 Lena: do you have quantized model suggestions for our use case? we typically use 8-bit quantization.
06:26 Ethan: yes, we have recommended quantization profiles by model family and sequence length. we'll share model-recommendations.xlsx. some models keep quality better with 4-bit quantization depending on the workload, but we'll validate on your evals.
06:45 Priya: next steps recap: maya to send onboarding deck + security pack, ethan to prep private deployment checklist and sizing, carlos to share VPC diagram; priya to schedule weekly checkpoints.
06:58 Amir: i also want a bench run — can we test with anonymized dataset first?
07:06 Maya: absolutely. recommended approach: anonymize PHI fields, run pilot on hosted with short retention and audit logging, then evaluate for dedicated/private move.
07:18 Carlos: any specific ports or egress ips to allowlist?
07:22 Ethan: i'll send the list; we also have a whitepaper on network requirements.
07:30 Sofia: ok, how will support work during pilot?
07:35 Priya: you'll have CSM support and we can do SE office hours; for dedicated/private there's an enterprise support SLA option.
07:44 Lena: timeline — can we lock the pilot start for 2027-04-01?
07:48 Maya: yes, if we get the VPC diagram and security contact by 2027-03-16 we should be able to start integration the week of 3/22 and land pilot by early April.
07:59 Amir: that works.
08:05 Maya: any other questions?
08:08 Carlos: one more on encryption — do you support envelope encryption with customer keys?
08:12 Ethan: yes, envelope encryption with KMS is supported; we'll include the required IAM policies in the security pack.
08:20 Maya: all right i'll summarize and send artifacts. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with proposed deep-dive times.
08:30 Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional minor transcription errors, and speaker labels are a mixture of real names and roles. Shared artifacts referenced: onboarding-deck.pdf (link), security-pack.pdf (link), model-recommendations.xlsx (link), kv-cache-sizing.xlsx (link).
